passage: Diary. Rukmini here. Papa paid the deposit for the engineering coaching today and hugged me. I said yes to everything. I do love him. He works so hard at the bank so we can have choices. But part of me said yes because I'm afraid of seeing his face if I said no. I actually like biology, and last week I spent an hour reading about how rivers change course, just because. Aparna didi, who did engineering, rang tonight. "Do you want it, or do you just not want to disappoint Papa?" I said I didn't know. She said, "Then find out before you're twenty and it's too late to say." I'm going to try talking to Papa on Sunday. Not fighting. Just telling him honestly what I'm thinking.

qa.q: What did Papa pay for today?
qa.a: The deposit for the engineering coaching.

qa.q: Why did Rukmini say yes to everything, and what mixed motives does she admit?
qa.a: Rukmini loves Papa and is grateful, but is also afraid of seeing his face if Rukmini said no.

qa.q: What did Aparna didi's question help Rukmini see, and what plan follows?
qa.a: It helped Rukmini see that the answer isn't clear yet. The plan is to talk honestly with Papa on Sunday, without fighting, instead of silently resenting the path for years.

qa.q: How might Papa feel about Rukmini's decision to talk to him?
qa.a: Probably surprised and maybe worried, but likely relieved to learn Rukmini's real thoughts. He hugged Rukmini over the coaching, so he seems to want the best for his child.

grounding: The protagonist accepts a parent's chosen career path from love and fear, then plans an honest talk instead of silent resentment.

The coaching institute's brochure lay on the dining table in the Kothrud flat, the engineering entrance batch circled in red by Papa. Sumit's elder sister Anjali watched him flip it open and close it again.

"You'll join, na?" Mummy asked from the kitchen. "Papa has already spoken to them."

"Yes, Mummy." He said it the way he had said it since Class 8. He loved them. He also knew the quiet that would fall over dinner if he said anything else.

Later, on the balcony, Anjali asked, "Do you even like physics?"

Sumit was quiet. "I like making things. I like the design club. I don't know if that's engineering or something else."

"Then find out before you sign up for two years of it. Talk to them. Papa listens more than you think."

That night Sumit wrote two lists: what he enjoyed and what he feared. On Sunday, over breakfast, he asked his parents if they could talk about both before he joined.

qa.q: What had Papa circled in red on the brochure?
qa.a: Papa had circled the engineering entrance batch in red.

qa.q: Why did Sumit say "Yes, Mummy" so quickly?
qa.a: He loved his parents but felt afraid of the tense silence at dinner if he disagreed, so fear and affection both pushed him to agree.

qa.q: What small step helped Sumit move towards an honest talk?
qa.a: Writing two lists, what he enjoyed and what he feared, helped him sort his thoughts before asking his parents to talk.

qa.q: How does Anjali see her brother's habit of agreeing?
qa.a: Anjali seems concerned that he is signing up for something he may not want, and believes their parents would listen if he spoke.

grounding: It shows a teen accepting the engineering path his family wants out of love and fear, then asking himself what he truly wants and planning an open talk.

"Papa, the medical coaching form. I filled it," Tushar said, sliding it across the table.

"Good boy." Papa didn't look up from the newspaper. "Dr Tushar. Your Dadi will cry with happiness."

Darshan, home from college for the weekend, put down his cup. "Tushar, you fainted at your own blood test last year."

"Bhaiya—"

"I'm just saying. Do you want this, or is this for Papa?"

Papa lowered the paper. "What is this?"

Tushar's hands were cold. "I… I don't know, Papa. I don't hate biology. But I've never asked myself properly. I just said yes because you were so happy."

The room was silent. Then Papa folded the newspaper. "You thought I would be angry."

"A bit."

"I would rather be disappointed now than have you unhappy for ten years." He pushed the form back. "Think for a week. Talk to Darshan. Talk to your biology teacher. Then we'll decide together."

qa.q: What did Tushar slide across the table?
qa.a: Tushar slid the medical coaching form across the table.

qa.q: What was Tushar feeling when his hands went cold?
qa.a: Tushar felt afraid of Papa's anger and unsure of what he wanted, having agreed mostly to see Papa happy.

qa.q: What would you advise Tushar to do in the week Papa gave him?
qa.a: Tushar could honestly note what he enjoys and what worries him, including how he feels about blood, and talk to Darshan and his biology teacher.

qa.q: How might Papa feel when he realises Tushar agreed out of fear?
qa.a: Papa seems surprised and a little hurt, but also relieved to hear the truth now rather than after years of resentment.

grounding: It shows a teen accepting the medicine path his family wants partly from love and fear, and being helped to ask what he wants and talk openly.
